fullPassage: Most artificial neural networks used in present-day artificial intelligence, despite their millions of inputs, outputs, and adjustable parameters, operate just like our proverbial hunter: they observe their errors and use them to adjust their internal state in the direction that they feel is best able to reduce the errors. In many cases, such learning is tightly guided. We tell the network exactly which response it should have activated at the output ("it is a 1, not a 7"), and we know precisely in which direction to adjust the parameters if they lead to an error (a mathematical calculation makes it possible to know exactly which connections to modify when the network activates the output "7" too often in response to an image of the number 1). In machine learning parlance, this situation is known as "supervised learning" (because someone, who can be likened to a supervisor, knows the correct answer that the system must give) and "error backpropagation" (because error signals are sent back into the network in order to modify its parameters). The procedure is simple: I try an answer, I am told what I should have answered, I measure my error, and I adjust my parameters to reduce it. At each step, I make only a small correction in the right direction. That's why such computer-based learning can be incredibly slow: learning a complex activity, like playing Tetris, requires applying this recipe thousands, millions, even billions of times. In a space that includes a multitude of adjustable parameters, it can take a long time to discover the optimal setting for every nut and bolt.

In many cases, such learning is tightly guided. We tell the network exactly which response it should have activated at the output ("it is a 1, not a 7"), and we know precisely in which direction to adjust the parameters if they lead to an error (a mathematical calculation makes it possible to know exactly which connections to <u>modify</u> when the network activates the output "7" too often in response to an image of the number 1). In machine learning parlance, this situation is known as "supervised learning" (because someone, who can be likened to a supervisor, knows the correct answer that the system must give) and "error backpropagation" (because error signals are sent back into the network in order to modify its parameters). The procedure is simple: I try an answer, I am told what I should have answered, I measure my error, and I adjust my parameters to reduce it. At each step, I make only a small correction in the right direction. That's why such computer-based learning can be incredibly slow: learning a complex activity, like playing Tetris, requires applying this recipe thousands, millions, even billions of times. In a space that includes a multitude of adjustable parameters, it can take a long time to discover the optimal setting for every nut and bolt.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 modify와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: modify: 수정하다, 변경하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① preserve(보존하다): modify의 반대
❌ ② ignore(무시하다): 수정과 무관
❌ ③ repeat(반복하다): 의미가 다름
✅ ④ change(바꾸다): modify와 동의어 ← 정답
det.tip: modify=수정하다(syn: change, alter, adjust)

questions.passage:
(A) During the press conference, the mayor will <u>state</u> his official position on the new policy. Reporters are waiting for his clear and final answer.

(B) The network observes its errors and then adjusts its internal <u>state</u> little by little in order to reduce them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 state의 문맥적 의미가 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: state: (A) 진술하다/밝히다 (동사) (B) 상태 (명사)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 상태 - (B) 진술하다: (A)의 will state는 '진술하다'(동사)
❌ ② (A) 상태 - (B) 상태: (A)는 동사이므로 오류
❌ ③ (A) 진술하다 - (B) 진술하다: (B) internal state는 '상태'(명사)
✅ ④ (A) 진술하다 - (B) 상태: (A) 입장을 '밝히다'(동사), (B) 내부 '상태'(명사) ← 정답
det.tip: state: 동사=진술하다/밝히다, 명사=상태. will 뒤면 동사, internal(형용사) 뒤면 명사

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the state or condition of being wrong in conduct or judgement; a mistake"

det.korean: 행동이나 판단이 잘못된 상태; 실수
det.analysis:
✅ ① error(오류): 잘못됨/실수의 정의와 일치 ← 정답
❌ ② answer(답): 질문에 대한 응답
❌ ③ image(이미지): 시각적 형상
❌ ④ recipe(방법/조리법): 절차나 방법
det.tip: error=오류/실수. 신경망은 error(오류)를 관찰하고 줄이며 학습

questions.passage: That's why such computer-based learning can be incredibly slow: learning a complex activity, like playing Tetris, requires __________ (apply) this recipe thousands, millions, even billions of times.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: apply → applying: 동사 require는 목적어로 동명사를 취함
det.analysis: apply(동사원형) → applying(동명사). 'require + 동명사(V-ing)' 구조로, '~하는 것을 요구하다'의 의미. require는 뒤에 to부정사가 아니라 동명사를 목적어로 취하는 동사. require applying=적용하는 것을 요구하다
det.tip: require + V-ing(동명사). require applying this recipe=이 방법을 적용할 것을 요구하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: correct → correction: 관사 a와 형용사 small 뒤에 오는 명사 형태
det.analysis: correct(동사/형용사) → correction(명사). 부정관사 a + 형용사 small 다음에는 명사가 와야 함. 'make a small correction'=작은 수정을 하다. 동사/형용사 correct를 명사 correction으로 전환
det.tip: a + 형용사 + 명사. correct → correction(명사). make a correction=수정하다

det.korean: 신경망은 오류를 관찰하고, 가장 잘 ______ 수 있다고 느끼는 방향으로 내부 상태를 조정한다 — '오류를 줄이다'
det.analysis:

det.analysis:

✅ ③ the optimal setting(최적의 설정): 수많은 매개변수 중 최적값을 찾는 데 시간이 오래 걸림 ← 정답
❌ ④ a random guess(무작위 추측): 최적값 탐색과 반대
det.tip: discover the optimal setting=최적의 설정을 발견하다. 매개변수가 많을수록 탐색에 시간 소요
